narrative_markdown:
## Today's Forecast

Slightly cooler and cloudier than yesterday; winds little changed. Largely dry, with thunder possible, peaking this evening. 31°C / 87°F high, 20°C / 68°F low. Sky mostly cloudy early as reported, mostly cloudy at midday and mostly cloudy in the evening. Wind NE early and NW in the evening; gusts to 41 km/h (22 kt). UV index 8.8 (very high). Air quality 47 (good) at Dunga Beach, the highest of 3 stations. As of 06:01, reports through 04:00: no rain; no thunder; high so far 23°C / 73°F; low so far 22°C / 72°F; peak sustained 11 km/h; sky mostly cloudy.

## Extended Outlook

Temperatures and winds much the same through Tuesday, with rain and thunderstorms likely each day. Skies mostly cloudy throughout. Rain gains support through Tuesday, from two of four models Sunday to all four models Tuesday. Tuesday's call: rain, 100%, with all four models wet; highs 29 to 31 °C. Kenya Meteorological Department (KMD) calls it wet. At this lead ICON has the best record, right 73% of the time over 70 checks.

Further out, temperatures and winds much the same through Saturday, with showers and thunderstorms likely Wednesday, Thursday and Friday, and showers and thunderstorms possible Saturday. Wednesday: all four models wet, highs 25 to 31 °C. Thursday: all four models wet, highs 27 to 30 °C. Friday: all three models that reach it wet, highs around 28 °C.

Only GFS, ECMWF and ICON reach past Thursday. ICON is the wetter solution from Wednesday to Thursday; GFS, ECMWF and UKMO keep it drier. Saturday's call: rain, 100%, with both models wet; highs around 29 °C. At this lead ECMWF has the best record, right 77% of the time over 66 checks.

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential

The high CAPE values today—UKMO at 4250 J/kg, ECMWF at 2360 J/kg, ICON at 1550 J/kg, and Best Match at 2570 J/kg—signal a thunderstorm risk with sudden gusts that could exceed the forecast wind. No specific bulletin from the Kenya Meteorological Department was issued, but the thunder possible, peaking this evening warning applies.

## Winam Gulf — Conditions for Boaters

Winam Gulf winds shift from a northeasterly 9 km/h (5 kt) gusting 12 km/h (7 kt) overnight, to 8 km/h (4 kt) gusting 18 km/h (10 kt) by midday, and then north-northwesterly 10 km/h (6 kt) gusting 18 km/h (10 kt) into the evening, with a peak gust of 30 km/h (16 kt). Thunderstorm gusts could be well above these values.

## Detailed Discussion

### Synoptic Overview

Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the north (1007 hPa) and highest toward the southeast (1014 hPa) — a 7 hPa spread, a moderate large-scale gradient. Pressure overhead is near-steady. Sampling is a nine-point ring at 12-degree spacing, so this locates a direction, not a centre or a front. Across the basin's 5 points, pressure today sits between 1012.3 and 1014.6 hPa, near-steady over three days (-0.6 hPa). Pressure here over the last 24 hours: -0.1 hPa.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes

Review notes that at Day+0 no model is meaningfully better than the others, with 54 checks supporting this settled picture. The Best Match model slightly under-forecasts peak wind today, while ECMWF slightly under-forecasts daytime highs and peak wind. GFS tends to over-forecast cloud cover and daytime highs, and systematically under-forecasts peak wind. The Kenya Meteorological Department forecast aligns with the call on temperature but offers less detail on wind and rain probabilities. Data sufficiency is strong with 73 days reviewed for Day+0, providing confidence in the overall guidance.
